title: App Builder Rendered Evidence
description: What a build actually renders, captured from a real browser against a real preview. A compiling build is not evidence that a visual change is correct, so this is a first-class artifact with its own identity rather than a folder of screenshots. It is visual evidence only: a capture can show what a state looks like and can never prove that a journey completes. States a screenshot cannot establish are recorded as uncovered, with the reason, rather than left out.

buildRef.description: The generated workspace this evidence was captured from.

renderingSource.description: What was actually serving when these captures were taken. Required, because its absence is what made two separate review failures possible: a set that photographed the wrong document, and a set that photographed a development-only banner the built output does not contain. A picture cannot say which artifact produced it, so the evidence has to.

serverMode.description: A development server renders things no built output contains. Capturing one is legitimate for iteration and is never evidence about what ships.

artifact.description: The served directory, relative to the workspace where possible. Null for a development server, which serves no artifact.

artifactHash.description: A hash over every path and byte the artifact serves, so a set can be re-checked against the build it claims and a rebuild invalidates it.

uncovered.description: Every state the deterministic state matrix names that this evidence deliberately does not claim, each with the reason. Silence here would read as complete coverage.

designLint.description: The deterministic DesignLint report for the build these captures came from, so a reviewer sees what rules already settled before judging a picture. Null where the evidence was captured before any lint ran, which is not the same as clean.

clean.description: No violation. Warnings and recommendations do not make a build unclean.

aiReviewCandidates.description: What the rules deliberately do not judge, so a visual critic spends its budget on questions that need judgement rather than re-deriving what a rule settled.

evidenceKind.description: Fixed. A rendered capture is visual evidence; journey completion is proved by executable evidence and never by a picture of a page.

interaction.description: The deterministic interaction from the closed registry that produced this state, or null for the page as first rendered.

proves.description: What this capture is evidence of, stated so it cannot be read as more.

elementRefs.description: Element identity refs this capture shows, so visual evidence and Builder Element Identity address the same things.
